boundaries.label: Composition root — the only place the adapters are wired
Feature pack — features/<name>/{views,viewmodels,ports,assets} · WALL: the View never imports the SDK
Shared packages — sdk · core · ui-native · tokens
Platform adapters — the only code that touches a platform API

cards.title: The layer contract
items: View — render native components, forward events, navigation, a11y; it may import its ViewModel hook, the UI kit and platform rendering APIs, and nothing else
ViewModel — presentation state, commands, derived values and SDK orchestration; it may import the SDK, the ports and shared domain types, and never react-native, react-dom or a UI component
SDK — typed HTTP client, DTOs, error normalization and auth headers; it may import the core ports and types, and never React, React Native or any UI
Ports — platform capabilities behind an interface; a port belongs to the consumer and the composition root wires the adapter, so a use case depends on the SDK interface, not on a concrete client

cards.title: Feature packs and variants
items: a feature pack is features/<name>/{views,viewmodels,ports,assets}; the feature name matches the backend slice, the route module and the permission prefix
one monorepo, three apps — game, market and avatar — selected by APP_VARIANT with separate bundle IDs, permissions and store listings
shared packages are sdk, core, viewmodels, ui-native and tokens; each app imports only what it ships, and a variant that does not ship a feature does not bundle its native module or assets

cards.title: The walls are lint rules
items: no-restricted-imports for src/**/views/** and src/screens/**: the groups @/sdk, @/sdk/* and **/sdk/* are denied — the View never talks to the network
no-restricted-imports for src/**/viewmodels/**: react-native, react-dom and @/views are denied — the ViewModel stays platform-free
no-restricted-imports for src/sdk/**: react, react-native and @/session are denied — the SDK stays a plain TypeScript client

the same config pins react-hooks/rules-of-hooks and exhaustive-deps, the no-remote-code rules (no-eval, no-new-func, no-implied-eval), switch-exhaustiveness-check, no-floating-promises and a single logger

cards.title: A config exception is a contract change
items: when a change would cross a layer, re-cut the layout: move the logic to the layer that owns it; the rule is never to weaken or delete the lints to make a change pass

lints/check/ is the violation harness: one deliberate file per rule with an // expect:<rule> marker plus a clean control; scripts/check-lints.sh fails if a marked rule stays quiet, if anything unmarked fires, or if tsc --noEmit fails on the same files
tests/contracts pins the wording across SKILL.md, the reference digests, the README and the config in lockstep, so a drift between the skill and the machine gate fails CI
